title: Economist Isabella Weber advocates for affordable essentials to address inequality and democracy
content:
Isabella Weber, an economist, argues that economic policy should prioritize practical solutions over ideological purity, comparing the field’s current state to a dentist who refuses to treat a patient in pain. Speaking in the canteen of the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin, Weber noted that John Maynard Keynes first drew this dental analogy to highlight the inflexibility of economists when addressing societal issues.

Weber contends that the current economic status quo is "entirely unbearable" for the majority, citing extreme inequality and corporate concentration that she describes as "simply incompatible with democracy" worldwide. She further states that the climate crisis is exacerbating these problems by causing the "ecological foundations of our lives [to] disintegrate" while generating "massive windfall profits" for big business.

According to Weber, these conditions are creating an environment where the far right is gaining traction. She proposes a common-sense solution to address poverty, inequality, and fascism by making life’s essentials affordable for all, asserting that people’s dignity and democracy are at stake.
summary: Economist Isabella Weber argues that making life's essentials affordable for all is a necessary solution to poverty, inequality, and the rise of fascism. She contends that extreme inequality and corporate concentration are incompatible with democracy, while the climate crisis generates windfall profits for big business.
author: Guardian Business

title: Massive black hole far from galaxy center shreds star in tidal disruption event
content:
Astronomers have discovered a star being torn apart by a massive black hole more than 1,000 parsecs from the center of its host galaxy. The event, designated TDE 2023mfm, was first identified by the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF).  

Follow‑up observations were carried out with a range of telescopes, including Keck, Lick, Hubble, Swift, Chandra, XMM‑Newton, and the Very Large Array (VLA). These studies confirmed the tidal disruption of the star by the distant black hole.  

The discovery paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on September 28.
summary: Astronomers identified a star being torn apart by a massive black hole located over 1,000 parsecs from its host galaxy's center. The event, designated TDE 2023mfm, was initially detected by ZTF and subsequently analyzed using multiple telescopes including Keck, Hubble, and Chandra.

title: AI and DNA-based mapping identify sewer pipes at risk of corrosion
content:
Underground sewer systems are critical for modern cities but present challenges for maintenance due to their inaccessible nature. Traditional camera inspections, while necessary to prevent aging pipes from deteriorating to the point of failure, are often costly and time-consuming.

The source highlights the risks associated with poor monitoring, noting that damaged pipes can leak and contaminate surrounding water, posing serious threats to public health. In more severe cases, pipe failures can damage infrastructure above ground, resulting in sinkholes on city streets.
summary: AI and wastewater DNA-based mapping help identify sewer pipes at risk of corrosion. Underground sewers manage wastewater but are hard to monitor, and damaged pipes can pose serious public health risks.

title: MPZPM study shows mechanical stress regulates muscle cell fusion
content:
Skeletal muscles grow and regenerate through a process where individual precursor cells, known as myoblasts, fuse into long fibers that develop into mature muscle fibers. Despite this mechanism, the exact way these cells coordinate to form functional muscles remains incompletely understood.

A research team at the Max-Planck-Zentrum für Physik und Medizin (MPZPM) has demonstrated that mechanical stress plays a role in regulating the fusion of muscle cells.
summary: A research team at the Max-Planck-Zentrum für Physik und Medizin has shown that mechanical stress influences the fusion of muscle cells. This finding addresses how myoblasts coordinate to form functional muscles during growth and regeneration.

content:

title: Combined sewer overflows in Philadelphia threaten water quality
content:
Philadelphia’s sewer infrastructure, which dates back to the 1800s, presents challenges for water quality as increased flooding threatens local ecosystems. In these urban areas, stormwater and sewage are channeled into the same pipes.

To prevent streets from inundating during heavy rain, these combined systems are designed to overflow into nearby waterways. This mechanism, known as combined sewer overflows, directly impacts the quality of surrounding aquatic environments.
summary: In Philadelphia, stormwater and sewage share the same pipes, which spill into nearby waterways during flooding. These combined sewer overflows pose a threat to people, property, and surrounding ecosystems.

content:

Since 1972, officials have added 27 leap seconds to the universal clock. The decision will end the practice of inserting these adjustments.

title: Scientists Find Gene DEAF1 Drives Muscle Aging; Exercise Reverses Damage
content:
Scientists have identified a biological mechanism that explains how exercise can reverse some damage associated with muscle aging. The discovery centers on a gene called DEAF1, which becomes overactive as people age and hampers the muscles’ ability to clear damaged proteins and repair themselves.

Research shows that exercise can restore the balance disrupted by the overactive DEAF1 gene. By doing so, older muscles are able to rebuild and regain strength, although the benefits may lessen when the system becomes too disrupted.

The findings highlight the role of DEAF1 in muscle aging and suggest that maintaining regular physical activity can mitigate its harmful effects.
summary: Scientists discovered that the gene DEAF1 becomes overactive with age and impairs muscle protein clearance and repair. Exercise restores balance, allowing older muscles to rebuild and regain strength, though benefits may lessen when the system is too disrupted.

title: USC scientists develop renewable supply of genetically engineered cancer‑fighting cells
content:
USC scientists have discovered a way to create a potentially renewable supply of genetically engineered immune cells that can attack cancer and strengthen the body's natural defenses.  

By growing and modifying immature immune cells rather than mature ones, researchers developed a system that can continuously produce tumor‑fighting cells inside the body.
summary: USC scientists have discovered a way to create a potentially renewable supply of genetically engineered immune cells that can attack cancer. They achieved this by growing and modifying immature immune cells instead of mature ones, enabling continuous production of tumor‑fighting cells inside the body.

title: Scientists Turn Cancer‑Fueling Protein PPARD into Immune Weapon Against Multiple Tumors
content:
Scientists have discovered a way to repurpose a protein that normally fuels cancer growth into a therapeutic tool. By activating the protein PPARD in immune cells, researchers enhanced the cells’ ability to burn fat and attack tumors, slowing or stopping cancer growth in laboratory experiments.

The approach showed promise against colorectal, breast, and ovarian cancers, as well as melanoma.
summary: Scientists discovered that activating the protein PPARD in immune cells enhances their ability to burn fat and attack tumors, slowing or stopping cancer growth in laboratory experiments. The approach showed promise against colorectal, breast, ovarian cancers, and melanoma.

content:

The images, described as extraordinary, show the powerful hurricane disturbing the upper atmosphere, creating patterns that are usually invisible from space.  

The rare footage highlights how intense tropical cyclones can affect atmospheric layers far above the surface.

title: Scientists find Nazi Germany's final reactor far from operational
content:
Scientists investigating Nazi Germany’s secret nuclear program have uncovered evidence that its final experimental reactor was nowhere near as close to working as previously claimed.  

Analysis of surviving uranium cubes and wartime documents reveals that Germany lacked the enormous quantities of uranium and heavy water needed to make its reactor operational.  

The findings clarify that the program did not reach a functional reactor stage.
summary: Scientists investigating Nazi Germany's secret nuclear program uncovered evidence that its final experimental reactor was nowhere near as close to working as previously claimed. Analysis of surviving uranium cubes and wartime documents shows Germany lacked the enormous quantities of uranium and heavy water needed to make its reactor operational.

content:

Scientists concluded that North American crayfish appear to hit a biological size limit, possibly due to constraints in their muscles or protective shells.
summary: Scientists discovered a record‑breaking Tennessee specimen during a nationwide search for giant crayfish. The study suggests North American crayfish may have a biological size limit due to muscle or shell constraints.

NGC 1827 lies roughly 37 million light‑years from Earth in the constellation Columba, also known as the Dove. The image highlights the galaxy’s edge‑on perspective, providing a clear view of its spiral arms and central bulge.
summary: The NASA Hubble Space Telescope captured an image of the edge‑on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827. The galaxy is located roughly 37 million light‑years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove.

content:

The device combines a retinal implant with camera-equipped eyeglasses to improve sight in patients with the disease.

title: BIPM votes to scrap leap seconds effective May 2026
content:
The International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM) voted on Thursday to eliminate the leap second, an occasional time adjustment used to keep tracked time standards aligned with the Earth’s inconsistent rotation. The change aims to prevent potential infrastructure failures similar to the Y2K bug scare.

While BIPM members had previously agreed in 2022 to cease using leap seconds on or before 2035, the decision has been expedited to take effect on May 20th of next year. This new date aligns with World Metrology Day.
summary: The International Bureau of Weights and Measures voted to discontinue the use of leap seconds to prevent potential infrastructure failures. This change is being expedited to take effect on May 20th next year, aligning with World Metrology Day.

title: Cody Wilson Unveils First AI‑Made 3D‑Printed Gun, the WASP
content:
The first vibe‑coded gun is here

Gun‑rights activist and alt‑right‑friendly agitator Cody Wilson, who created the first 3D‑printed firearm 13 years ago, has announced a new device he calls the WASP, claiming it to be “the first AI‑made gun.” The weapon was displayed outside Defense Distributed headquarters in Austin, Texas, where Wilson and a sidekick clamped the WASP onto a DIY test mount while the author stood about 20 feet away.

The WASP is a 3D‑printed .22 caliber handgun that essentially consists of a pistol barrel attached to a spring‑loaded plastic box. Its rudimentary design resembles Wilson’s single‑shot 3D‑printed “Liberator,” though it incorporates additional features. The full story is available at The Verge.

content:

The device, launched more than two years ago with a Qualcomm Snapdragon 6 Gen 1 chipset and Android 14, had been slated for three major OS upgrades, including the current Android 17 release.

A notice posted to Sony’s UK support site explains that a detailed technical assessment found limitations related to the Xperia 10 VI’s storage configuration. These limitations mean the phone does not support an Android 17 upgrade experience that Sony considers adequate. As a result, the company has decided not to make the Android 17 upgrade available for the Xperia 10 VI.
summary: Sony promised the mid‑range Xperia 10 VI three major OS updates, including Android 17, when it launched with Android 14. A technical assessment of the device’s storage configuration led Sony to decide the phone will not support an adequate Android 17 upgrade.

content:

The foldable model is scheduled to hit retail stores on October 23rd, and Apple typically keeps a portion of units for in‑store availability. While online orders remain delayed, customers may obtain a device sooner by purchasing in person at an Apple Store. The extended wait could stem from high demand for Apple’s first foldable iPhone, limited supply on Apple’s side, or a combination of both.

Apple announced the iPhone Duo in September.

content:

title: Antibiotic Resistance in Nairobi Gut Bacteria Displaces Healthy Microbes
content:

Years of antibiotic use have fueled a rise in bacteria that can survive antibiotics. In a Nairobi community, these antibiotic‑resistant bacteria are competing with and displacing other bacteria that are naturally present in the human gut, where they play a critical role in maintaining good health.

The displacement of natural gut bacteria by resistant strains has led to increased illness and death from diseases that were once easily treatable with antibiotics.

title: Syria arrests Ali Kayali, accused of 2013 Bayda and Baniyas civilian killings
content:
Syria announced the arrest of Ali Kayali, a 70‑year‑old militia commander known as “Mihrac Ural.” The security operation targets the individual accused of leading al‑Assad‑affiliated forces that carried out mass killings along the coast.

According to authorities, Kayali’s militia conducted summary executions of more than 450 civilians in the towns of Bayda and Baniyas during May 2013. The arrests come as part of ongoing efforts to hold those responsible for the 2013 coastal massacres accountable.
summary: Syria arrested 70‑year‑old Ali Kayali, also known as Mihrac Ural. He commanded al‑Assad‑affiliated militia forces that carried out summary executions of more than 450 civilians in Bayda and Baniyas in May 2013.
author: Euronews

title: Germany to raise tobacco tax, aiming for cigarette packs near €12 by 2030
content:
Germany plans to raise its tobacco tax, a move that could push the price of a pack of cigarettes to nearly €12 by 2030, according to the proposal outlined in the title.  

The government estimates that the tax increase will generate an additional €12 billion in revenue over the next four years.  

The projected price rise and revenue target are part of the same fiscal plan aimed at strengthening the country's tax base.
summary: Germany plans to increase its tobacco tax, which could push the price of a pack of cigarettes to close to €12 by 2030. The government expects the tax hike to raise an additional €12 billion over four years.
author: Euronews

title: Families of 34 children killed in Pakistan school roof collapse demand justice
content:
Families of 34 children killed in a school roof collapse in Pakistan are demanding justice for the tragedy.  

A senior official in Peshawar told AFP that initial reports indicated the collapse was caused by “weak infrastructure.”  

The demand for accountability follows the deaths of the 34 children in the incident.
summary: Families of 34 children killed in a school roof collapse in Pakistan are demanding justice. A senior official in Peshawar said initial reports linked the collapse to weak infrastructure.
author: Euronews

title: Ukraine's SkyFall unveils StarGate drone that transports wounded soldiers
content:
Ukraine has unveiled a flying ambulance drone that could save lives in minutes. The system was demonstrated by a Ukrainian company as a new battlefield rescue option.

Developed by SkyFall, the unmanned aircraft is called StarGate and is designed to carry a wounded soldier inside an enclosed cabin. The drone’s capacity to transport a person marks a departure from conventional medical evacuation methods.

The demonstration was filmed showing StarGate taking off, flying and landing with a person on board, illustrating its operational capabilities for rapid rescue missions.
summary: SkyFall demonstrated a battlefield rescue system featuring a drone that can carry a wounded soldier inside an enclosed cabin. The drone, named StarGate, was filmed taking off, flying and landing with a person on board.
author: Euronews

title: At least 12 killed when migrant boat sinks off Gambia
content:
At least 12 people died when a migrant boat sank off the coast of The Gambia, according to reports.

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) said that tighter controls at traditional departure points in Morocco, Mauritania and Senegal have forced some migrants seeking to reach Europe to travel farther south, including to countries such as The Gambia.
summary: At least 12 people died after a migrant boat sank off the coast of The Gambia. The IOM said tighter controls in Morocco, Mauritania and Senegal have pushed migrants toward The Gambia.
author: Euronews

title: Marseille lose 1-0 to Olympiakos for second straight Europa League defeat
content:
Marseille’s woes continued in the Europa League as the French club suffered a second straight defeat, losing 1‑0 to Olympiakos. The loss marked the side’s second loss in as many Europa League matches.

In contrast, Lyon secured a victory over Premier League side Crystal Palace, while Rennes recorded their first Europa League win of the season with a 2‑1 triumph over OFI Crete.
summary: Marseille were beaten 1-0 by Olympiakos, marking their second consecutive Europa League loss. Lyon beat Crystal Palace and Rennes secured a 2-1 victory over OFI Crete.
author: France 24

title: UK bookstores stock up as Sally Rooney novels pulled over Palestine Action support
content:
UK bookstores are scrambling after critically acclaimed Irish novelist Sally Rooney announced that her books could no longer be sold in the United Kingdom because of her support for the proscribed group Palestine Action.  

Rooney’s statement has prompted British booksellers to rush to stock up on her titles before distributors run out.  

The British government has banned Palestine Action, which carried out non‑violent direct action and sabotage against UK military assets believed to be working with the Israeli government; support for the group is punishable by up to 14 years in prison.
summary: Sally Rooney announced that her books could no longer be sold in the UK because of her support for the proscribed group Palestine Action. British booksellers are rushing to stock up on her works before distributors run out, and support for Palestine Action carries a penalty of up to 14 years in prison under the British government's ban.
author: France 24

title: Democrats eye Latino regret ahead of 2026 midterms after Trump’s 2024 support drops
content:
In the 2024 presidential election, 46 percent of the Latino vote helped Donald Trump win the White House. Polls taken two years later show that Latino support for Trump has fallen dramatically, with many voters citing an immigration crackdown, violent ICE raids and a spiraling cost of living as reasons for their regret.

As the 2026 midterm elections approach, Democrats are looking to recapture this segment of the electorate that once formed a core part of their base. France 24 reporters Sam Ball and Barbara Gabel interviewed Latino voters and local Democratic officials in Phoenix, Arizona, to assess whether the expressed regret among Latino voters could translate into renewed Democratic support.
summary: In 2024, a 46 percent share of the Latino vote helped propel Donald Trump to the White House. Polls two years later show Latino support for Trump has fallen sharply, with some voters expressing regret and Democrats looking to use that sentiment in the 2026 midterms.
author: France 24

title: Indian authorities close central Delhi park ahead of Cockroach Janta Party rally
content:
Indian authorities have closed a central park in the Indian capital and heightened security ahead of a rally by the youth‑led “Cockroach Janta Party.”  

The group has staged near‑daily demonstrations demanding the resignation of the national election authority chief, citing the removal of more than 130 million people from voter lists. The park closure is part of the authorities’ security measures surrounding the upcoming protest.
summary: Authorities closed a central park in the Indian capital before a protest by the youth‑led Cockroach Janta Party. The group has staged near‑daily demonstrations demanding the national election authority chief’s resignation over the removal of more than 130 million people from voter lists.
author: France 24

title: Students join Yellow Vest protest in Montbéliard, union leader questions alliance impact
content:
Students have joined the nationwide Yellow Vest demonstrations as their protests merge with broader public discontent over France’s rising cost of living.  

Genie Godula is speaking alongside Sébastien Vieille, national secretary of the SNALC teachers’ union, who says the movement faces political uncertainty, deteriorating school infrastructure and mounting fiscal constraints.  

From Montbéliard in eastern France, Vieille questioned whether aligning with larger protest movements such as the Yellow Vests will give students greater collective strength or cause their demands to become “less visible.”
summary: Student protests have merged with the broader Yellow Vest movement in France over the rising cost of living. SNALC teachers’ union national secretary Sébastien Vieille, speaking in Montbéliard, said the alliance could either strengthen students’ demands or make them less visible.
author: France 24

title: Russian tanker was carrying fertilizer, not diesel, to U.S. after Trump‑Putin diesel deal
content:
Following President Donald Trump’s October 9 announcement of an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel into the United States, several pro‑Russian social‑media accounts asserted that a Russian oil tanker was already transporting thousands of barrels of diesel to the United States.

Investigations confirmed that the vessel in question was not carrying diesel but was instead loaded with fertiliser. The claim that the tanker was delivering Russian diesel to the U.S. was therefore inaccurate.
summary: After President Donald Trump's October 9 announcement of a diesel import agreement with President Vladimir Putin, pro‑Russian social media accounts claimed a Russian oil tanker was transporting diesel to the United States. The ship was actually carrying fertilizer, not diesel.
author: France 24

title: France to see mass protests on Saturday, described as a “crossroads of anger”
content:
France is poised to see a “crossroads of anger” on Saturday, as French newspapers report a call for mass protests that will unite a number of social movements. The preview appeared in a press review dated Friday, October 16.

The scheduled demonstrations are expected to bring together multiple groups, though specific organizers or turnout figures were not disclosed.
summary: French newspapers say Saturday will see mass protests that will bring together a number of social movements. The protests have been described as a “crossroads of anger.”
author: France 24

title: Carney says US trying to 'break' Canada as Alberta votes on independence
content: Alberta, the oil‑rich western province, is set to hold a vote that will decide whether it remains a Canadian province or begins a legal process toward separation. The referendum follows comments from Carney, who has implied that the United States is trying to “break” Canada amid the upcoming vote. The outcome of the Alberta referendum will determine the province’s future relationship with the rest of the country.
summary: Carney implied the United States is trying to “break” Canada. Alberta will vote to decide whether to remain a Canadian province or start the legal process toward separation.
author: DW World

title: Palestinian man wanders Gaza after Israeli strike kills his family
content:
A Palestinian man is wandering the Gaza Strip in search of a place to sleep after an Israeli strike killed his family. The loss has left him without relatives or a home.

The situation is described as “genocide” in the headline, highlighting that the man now faces life alone in Gaza with no shelter.
summary: A man is wandering Gaza searching for a place to sleep. He lost his family in an Israeli strike.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Vibe coding enables AI-built software, but free alternatives raise security concerns
content:
Vibe coding, a new AI‑driven tool that enables users to build software, is being highlighted as a potential breakthrough in development workflows.  

However, the emergence of free alternatives to established programming applications has prompted security concerns, as analysts caution that such options may lack robust safeguards.  

The debate centers on whether Vibe coding’s capabilities outweigh the risks associated with less‑secure, cost‑free software solutions.
summary: Vibe coding lets users build software with AI. Free alternatives to popular programmes raise security concerns.
author: Al Jazeera

title: World Food Day: Over a billion tonnes of food wasted while 645 million go hungry
content:
On World Food Day, officials highlighted that 645 million people are currently going hungry while more than a billion tonnes of food are wasted each year.

The stark contrast between global hunger and the scale of food loss underscores the need for actions to address waste, though specific country rankings or household‑level recommendations were not detailed in the report.
summary: On World Food Day, 645 million people are going hungry. More than a billion tonnes of food are wasted each year.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Netanyahu's lasting legacy seen as right‑wing opposition ahead of Israeli polls
content:
As Israel heads to the polls, analysts note that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s most enduring domestic legacy may be the right‑wing opposition he has forged.

The observation highlights the prominence of a right‑wing bloc that now stands in opposition to Netanyahu as the country prepares for its upcoming election.
summary: Israel is heading to the polls. PM Netanyahu's most enduring domestic legacy may be the right‑wing opposition he faces.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel's upcoming election to shape future of 5.5 million Palestinians
content:
Israel is holding national elections this month.  

The outcome of the vote is expected to shape the future of more than 5.5 million Palestinians, a population that does not participate in the election.  

These Palestinians have no say in the electoral process, yet the results will affect their lives.
summary: Israel is voting this month. The result will affect the future of over 5.5 million Palestinians who have no say in the election.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Zelensky seeks EU support as Trump calls him harder to deal with than Putin
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is seeking backing from European Union leaders ahead of their summit in Brussels, while U.S. President Donald Trump has launched a fresh wave of criticism against him. Trump described Zelensky as “more difficult to deal with than Putin,” intensifying the verbal dispute between the two leaders.

The president’s remarks come just before the EU leaders’ meeting in Brussels, where Zelensky is expected to rally support for Ukraine. Trump's comments add a new dimension to the diplomatic environment surrounding the summit.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is rallying EU support ahead of a meeting of EU leaders in Brussels. US President Trump launched blistering criticism, saying Zelensky is more difficult to deal with than Putin.
author: BBC World

title: Record-high ship attacks near Hormuz see 12 vessels struck in one week
content:
Ship attack reports near the Strait of Hormuz have reached a record high, coinciding with a slowdown in oil exports, according to the article’s headline.  

BBC Verify’s analysis of data from a UK maritime agency found that 12 vessels were struck in a single week, indicating a sharp increase in reported attacks in the region.
summary: Reports of ship attacks near the Strait of Hormuz reached a record high, with 12 vessels reported struck in a week, according to BBC Verify analysis of UK maritime agency data. The surge in attacks coincided with a slowdown in oil exports.
author: BBC World

title: Rocket Lab Delays Neutron Launch Vehicle to 2027 Due to Carbon Fibre Issues
content:
Rocket Lab has postponed the debut of its Neutron launch vehicle to no earlier than 2027. The delay follows ongoing issues with the manufacturing of carbon fibre components used in the rocket.

The company cited persistent carbon fibre production problems as the reason for the new schedule. This marks a second postponement of the Neutron launch vehicle.

The information was reported by NASA SpaceFlight.
summary: Rocket Lab has delayed its Neutron launch vehicle again because of carbon fibre manufacturing problems. The new debut date is no earlier than 2027.
author: NASASpaceFlight

title: Denver Broncos defeat Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in OT, Darnold intercepted twice
content:
The Denver Broncos defeated the defending Super Bowl champions Seattle Seahawks 17‑14 in overtime on Thursday night.  Wil Lutz capped the win with a 53‑yard field goal after the game went into the extra period.

Seattle’s quarterback Darnold was intercepted twice late in the game, costing the Seahawks the victory.  The Broncos’ win improves their record to 4‑2 for the season‑opening stretch, despite an injury‑ridden roster and a struggling offense.

The Seahawks fall to 3‑3, losing for the second time in five days.  Their loss total matches the 3‑3 record they posted last season when they captured their second Super Bowl title.
summary: The Denver Broncos defeated the Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime, with Wil Lutz kicking a 53‑yard field goal. Quarterback Darnold was intercepted twice late in the game, and the Broncos improved to a 4‑2 record while the Seahawks fell to 3‑3.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Martin O'Neill defiant after Celtic lose twice in Europa League
content:
Celtic have now lost two Europa League group games and two derbies, leaving the club on a difficult run of results.  

Despite the defeats, manager Martin O’Neill remains defiant, insisting he can see positive signs in the team’s performance.  

The club’s nickname, “flat‑track bullies,” has once again failed a big test, according to the club’s own assessment.
summary: Celtic have lost two Europa League group games and two derbies. Martin O'Neill says he can see positive signs.
author: BBC Sport

title: FDA submits peptide interim access policy to White House
content:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has submitted a peptide “interim access policy” to the White House for review, according to a government filing. The policy would allow compounding pharmacies to temporarily produce and sell peptides that have previously been restricted.

The filing was presented by the Coalition to Strengthen America’s Healthcare. The policy is part of a broader effort to expand access to peptide therapies, with the FDA seeking executive review before any changes are implemented.

The White House has not yet issued a response to the FDA’s proposal.
summary: The Food and Drug Administration this week submitted a peptide “interim access policy” to the White House for review, according to a government filing. The policy would reportedly allow compounding pharmacies to temporarily produce and sell previously restricted peptides.
author: The Hill

title: Noem no longer serves as special envoy to Shield of the Americas
content:
Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem is no longer serving as the Trump administration’s special envoy to the “Shield of the Americas” coalition, the State Department confirmed.

State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott told NewsNation, The Hill’s broadcasting partner, that Noem’s time had come to… in an interview with NewsNation’s Kellie Meyer on Thursday evening.

The confirmation was issued by the State Department spokesperson.
summary: State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott confirmed that Kristi Noem is no longer serving as the special envoy to the Shield of the Americas coalition. Pigott made this statement in an interview with NewsNation on Thursday evening.
author: The Hill

title: Collins and Jackson trade jabs in final Maine Senate debate
content:
Sen. Susan Collins (R‑Maine) faced off against Democratic candidate Troy Jackson on Thursday in the final Senate debate before Maine voters head to the polls. The two candidates traded jabs over President Trump, campaign financing, immigration reform and their voting record as the Senate race enters its final stretch.

Collins highlighted her bipartisan approach to voting during the exchange, while Jackson countered on the same issues. The debate marked the last opportunity for voters to hear directly from the candidates before casting their ballots.
summary: Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic candidate Troy Jackson held their final Senate debate before Maine voters head to the polls. The candidates exchanged criticism regarding President Trump, campaign financing, immigration reform, and their voting records.
author: The Hill

title: Massie urges Trump to fire Hegseth before impeachment vote
content: Rep. Thomas Massie (R‑Ky.) urged President Trump to remove Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth before the House moves to vote on impeachment. The Kentucky Republican, who often finds himself in the crosshairs of Trump for frequently breaking with the party, made the comment in response to a report claiming the president was considering firing the defense secretary.
summary: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) said President Trump should remove Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth before the House votes to impeach him. He responded to a report claiming Trump was considering firing Hegseth.
author: The Hill

title: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia Confirms She Did Not Pass Bar Exam
content:
Katie Zacharia, the White House press secretary, confirmed late Thursday that she had not passed the bar exam. The statement came after questions arose about her legal background before she joined the Trump administration.

Zacharia had previously claimed to be a lawyer and President Trump had referred to her as an “attorney.” Her qualifications were scrutinized during her first week in the role.
summary: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said she did not pass the bar exam. Her legal background was questioned after she joined the Trump administration.
author: The Hill

title: Longer Sleep Duration Linked to Higher Risk of Diabetic Nephropathy in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes
content: A recent study published online on Oct. 8 in the Journal of the Endocrine Society found that adults with type 2 diabetes who sleep longer have a higher risk of developing diabetic nephropathy and of experiencing its progression. The research links extended sleep duration with increased incidence and worsening of kidney disease in this population.
summary: A study published online Oct. 8 in the Journal of the Endocrine Society found that adults with type 2 diabetes who sleep longer have an increased risk for incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy. The study links longer sleep duration with a higher risk of both developing and worsening diabetic nephropathy among adults with type 2 diabetes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds undeclared active ingredients in one-third of online OTC skin products
content:
A recent study published online on Oct. 8 in JAMA Network Open reports that undeclared pharmacologically active ingredients (UPAIs) were detected in one‑third of over‑the‑counter (OTC) skin products sold online.

The research highlights a significant presence of unlisted active compounds in a substantial portion of OTC skin products available through online marketplaces.
summary: Undeclared pharmacologically active ingredients (UPAIs) are detected in one-third of over-the-counter skin products marketed online. The finding was reported in a study published online Oct. 8 in JAMA Network Open.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Online sports betting linked to increased depression and anxiety treatment
content:
Online sports betting linked to rise in depression and anxiety treatment

More people are receiving treatment for depression and anxiety in states that legalized online sports betting.

The increase in mental‑health care usage is reported specifically in states where online sports betting has been legalized.
summary: States that legalized online sports betting see more people receiving treatment for depression and anxiety. The increase in treatment correlates with the legalization of online sports betting.
author: Medical Xpress

title: American Journal of Gastroenterology Publishes Cirrhosis Preventive Care Guidelines
content:
Recommendations developed for preventive care in cirrhosis

Clinical guidelines detailing preventive care for patients with cirrhosis were published online on Oct. 5 in the American Journal of Gastroenterology. The guidelines outline new recommendations for managing and preventing complications in this patient population.
summary: Recommendations have been developed for preventive care of patients with cirrhosis, according to clinical guidelines published online Oct. 5 in the American Journal of Gastroenterology.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Same-day Metagenomics Test Detects Hidden Infections in Critically Ill Children
content:
Same‑day testing is now helping doctors identify hidden infections in critically ill children. The new approach allows clinicians to quickly detect pathogens that may otherwise go unnoticed in intensive care settings.

Metagenomics offers a new way of detecting infections in intensive care patients.
summary: A same-day test helps doctors detect hidden infections in critically ill children. Metagenomics offers a new way of detecting infections in intensive care patients.
author: BBC Health

title: Animated films still feature overwhelmingly male nonhuman characters
content:
Female protagonists in animated films have evolved significantly over the past several decades. The 1959 Disney classic Sleeping Beauty illustrates early portrayals of women in animation.

In Sleeping Beauty, Princess Aurora is depicted as soft‑spoken and vulnerable. She is cursed as an infant by the evil fairy Maleficent and ultimately rescued not by her own wits but by a prince's kiss.
summary: Female protagonists in animated films have progressed over decades. In the 1959 film Sleeping Beauty, Princess Aurora is cursed by Maleficent and ultimately saved by a prince's kiss.
author: Phys.org

title: OSU Student Finds Extra Weight May Impact Dogs' Brain Health
content:
Scientists are expanding their understanding of aging beyond humans, focusing now on dogs. Research suggests that carrying extra weight may impact a dog's cognitive health, highlighting the need for further study.

Alexandra Genualdi, a student at Oklahoma State University, presented her findings at the American Physiological Society’s 2026 Comparative Physiology conference in Orlando in September. Genualdi discussed her efforts to investigate how obesity affects canine brain function.

The study underscores that while human aging has been extensively studied, the effects of weight on dogs’ cognitive health remain an emerging area of research.
summary: Scientists have learned a lot about human aging, but still need to learn more about how other species age, including dogs. Alexandra Genualdi, an Oklahoma State University student, presented research in September at the American Physiological Society's 2026 Comparative Physiology conference in Orlando, showing that carrying extra weight could affect a dog's cognitive health.
author: Phys.org

title: Barn owl family nests in Upper West Side water tower near Central Park
content:
A rare family of barn owls has moved into Manhattan’s Upper West Side, nesting in a water tower atop a building near Central Park. The owls have taken residence in the high‑rise structure, creating a new point of interest for residents and visitors.

New Yorkers are captivated by the unexpected visitors, watching the owls from balconies and street corners as they settle into their new urban habitat.
summary: A family of barn owls has nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park on Manhattan's Upper West Side. Residents of the Upper West Side have been reveling in the birds' presence.
author: Phys.org

title: Canada’s endangered species face extensive delays in protection under SARA
content:
Endangered species in Canada are encountering extensive delays in receiving protection, according to recent reporting.  

For more than 20 years, Canada’s Species at Risk Act (SARA) has served as the legal framework for safeguarding wildlife at risk of loss from Canadian lands and waters. Under the act, once a species is classified as extirpated, endangered or threatened, it becomes illegal to kill, harm or capture the animal, to damage its residences, and its critical habitat must be protected, at least on federal land.  

The ongoing delays in listing and protecting species highlight challenges in the implementation of SARA’s protections.
summary: Endangered species in Canada face extensive delays in receiving protection. Under the Species at Risk Act, listed species become illegal to kill, harm or capture, and their critical habitat must be protected on federal land.
author: Phys.org

title: Professor Damian Helbling creates first detailed map of PFAS in Finger Lakes
content:
A first in‑depth map of per‑ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the Finger Lakes region has been produced, highlighting the presence of the so‑called “forever chemicals” in local water bodies. The effort was led by professor Damian Helbling, who in 2023 began receiving a surge of calls and emails from Ithacan residents and others after the Environmental Protection Agency announced new regulations to limit PFAS in drinking water.

Residents asked about PFAS levels in the ponds, lakes, streams and creeks near their homes, prompting Helbling’s team to compile detailed measurements across the watershed. The resulting map provides the most comprehensive view to date of PFAS contamination in the Finger Lakes area.
summary: In 2023, professor Damian Helbling began receiving calls after the EPA announced new limits on PFAS in drinking water. He produced the first in‑depth map of PFAS contamination in the Finger Lakes region’s ponds, lakes, streams and creeks.
author: Phys.org

title: BeBox is a Haiku app that emulates Be Inc.'s BeBox
content:
BeBox, a Haiku operating system application, replicates the functionality of the original Be Inc. BeBox computer. The project is hosted on GitHub at https://github.com/johnrash/bebox.

The application has drawn attention on Hacker News, receiving 35 points and generating nine comments on the discussion thread (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50111742).
summary: BeBox is a Haiku application that emulates Be Inc.'s BeBox. The project is hosted on GitHub and has received 35 points and 9 comments on Hacker News.
author: Hacker News

title: Meta to scrape business accounts' websites with consent starting Oct 30
content:
Meta announced that, beginning October 30, business accounts will be required to consent to the company’s scraping of their websites. The change applies to all business‑type accounts that use Meta’s platforms.

The new terms will allow Meta to collect data from the sites of consenting business accounts, according to the announcement. No further details about the scope or implementation were provided in the source.
summary: Business accounts will consent to Meta scraping their websites. The consent takes effect on Oct. 30.
author: Hacker News

title: Tool lets Mac windows appear on iPhone and iPad
content:
A GitHub repository titled “Any window from your Mac, on your iPhone and iPad” has been posted by the user Saffsanity. The project, named sill, is hosted at https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill.

The repository has attracted attention on Hacker News, earning 55 points and generating eight comments. The discussion thread is available at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50112739.
summary: An article on GitHub describes a way to view any Mac window on an iPhone and iPad. The post earned 55 points and eight comments on Hacker News.
author: Hacker News

title: Tesla unveils Roadster 2 with thrusters that can send it airborne
content:
Tesla unveiled its next luxury sports car, the Tesla Roadster 2, at an event in Texas. The automaker highlighted the vehicle’s new design and performance features during the presentation.

The Roadster 2 is equipped with thrusters that can send it airborne, showcasing the car’s ability to fly.
summary: The automaker unveiled its next luxury sports car at an event in Texas. It has thrusters on it that can send it airborne.
author: Wired

title: FAA to weigh in on Tesla Roadster 2’s potential to fly
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration is expected to weigh in on the Tesla Roadster 2’s potential to leave the ground, amid speculation about the vehicle’s capability as a flying car.  

The agency’s forthcoming comments will address whether the Roadster 2 meets aviation standards for any such operation.
summary: The Federal Aviation Administration is expected to comment on the Tesla Roadster 2. The agency’s input will address the vehicle’s ability to leave the ground.
author: Wired

title: Tesla Roadster demo in Texas flies, drives upside down and hits 0‑60 in under a second
content:
Tesla’s next‑generation Roadster was showcased in a brief, stunt‑style event in Waco, Texas, where the electric supercar drove upside down, briefly flew, and accelerated to 60 mph in under a second. The demonstration lasted less than 30 minutes and focused solely on performance, with no mention of price, release date, or other product details.

Elon Musk, who had previously promised a flying car, highlighted the Roadster’s capabilities during the Waco show. The event emphasized the vehicle’s extreme acceleration and airborne maneuvering, presenting the car as a hypercar rather than a conventional production model.

Musk has stated that the hypercar is slated for production in 2028, though the demonstration suggested that significant caveats and restrictions may accompany any future release.
summary: Tesla demonstrated its next‑generation Roadster at an event in Waco, Texas, where the electric supercar drove upside down, briefly flew, and accelerated to 60 mph in under a second. Elon Musk said the hypercar is slated for production in 2028, though the short stunt‑style show omitted price or release details.
author: The Verge

title: Tesla unveils SpaceX‑powered Roadster that leapt over vehicles in Texas demo
content:
Tesla unveiled a SpaceX‑powered Roadster described as a vehicle that “flies and falls with style.” The new car’s thrusters were demonstrated in Texas, where it leapt over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y and Model 3.  

The Texas demo highlighted the Roadster’s ability to use thrusters to clear multiple Tesla models in a single jump.
summary: Tesla revealed a SpaceX‑powered Roadster that can fly using thrusters. At a demo in Texas the car leapt over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y and Model 3.
author: TechCrunch

title: Four dead in Bend, Oregon elementary school shooting, including three children
content:
A 16‑year‑old opened fire at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, killing four people – three children aged 5, 8 and 11, and a teacher.  

The suspect was found dead at the scene. In addition to the fatalities, another child and a teacher were taken to the hospital with critical injuries.  

The shooting occurred at the Bend elementary school, leaving the community reeling from the loss of the three young students and the teacher.
summary: A 16-year-old opened fire at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, killing three children aged 5, 8 and 11 and a teacher. The shooter was found dead, and another child and a teacher were left critically injured.
author: Euronews

title: France and Germany agree to ease EU car emissions rules in new deal
content:
France and Germany have reached a provisional deal to loosen European Union emissions rules for carmakers. The agreement, announced on Thursday, also includes Britain in a “made in Europe” scheme.

The new arrangement, backed by both countries, could reshape the bloc’s automotive and climate policies by easing regulatory standards while extending the European‑made designation to the United Kingdom.
summary: France and Germany have backed looser EU emissions rules for carmakers and agreed to include Britain in a “made in Europe” scheme, in a provisional deal reached Thursday that could reshape the bloc’s automotive and…
author: France 24

title: 19 injured after minibus hits shuttle train at French Channel Tunnel entrance
content:
Nineteen people were injured on Thursday when a minibus carrying truck drivers collided with a vehicle shuttle train at the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel near Calais.

The crash forced a 90‑minute suspension of shuttle services through the tunnel. French authorities said two of the injured were hospitalised with serious but non‑life‑threatening injuries.
summary: Nineteen people were injured Thursday when a minibus carrying truck drivers crashed into a vehicle shuttle train at the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel near Calais. The crash forced a 90‑minute suspension of shuttle services and two people were hospitalised with serious but non‑life‑threatening injuries, French authorities said.
author: France 24

title: Trump calls Ukraine's renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries a disgrace
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump described Ukraine’s renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries as a “disgrace” after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky rejected Trump’s appeal for an “energy ceasefire.”  

Earlier in the day, Zelensky traveled to Brussels, where he sought support from European allies on the sidelines of an EU summit.  

The exchange was reported in a liveblog covering the developing situation.

title: Evanilson, Rayan and Rodríguez score as Bournemouth earn historic Europa League home win
content:
Bournemouth secured a historic home win in the Europa League at the Vitality Stadium, beating Sturm Graz 3‑1.  First‑half, Brazilian Evanilson headed home, followed by Rayan’s later drive, and a stoppage‑time penalty from Álvaro Rodríguez sealed the victory.  The win came after a recent away triumph at Real Sociedad and was the club’s first European win at home.

The result eased domestic pressure on manager Marco Rose, who has yet to win a Premier League match.  The stadium featured a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand that read “Minus 17 to European dreams,” and the public address system played Elvis Presley and Andy Williams.  Bournemouth’s financier, Bill Foley, was present in the posh seats.

Captain Adam Smith praised the supporters and players, saying, “A long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.”  The club will face Milan in the next round of the competition.
summary: Evanilson’s first‑half header, Rayan’s later strike and Álvaro Rodríguez’s stoppage‑time penalty gave Bournemouth a historic Europa League home victory over Sturm Graz at the Vitality Stadium. title: Heart failure reshapes bone marrow to create inflammation-related immune memory
content:
Heart failure (HF) affects the body beyond the heart’s pumping and circulation functions by inducing a lasting form of innate immune memory in bone marrow (BM). This condition specifically impacts stem cells responsible for synthesizing blood, as well as progenitor cells within the bone marrow.

The resulting immune memory leads to the production of immune cells that promote inflammation, which in turn worsens heart function. Despite these known consequences, the exact mechanism behind this process remains unclear.
summary: Heart failure causes a lasting form of innate immune memory in bone marrow stem and progenitor cells. This process leads to the production of immune cells that promote inflammation and worsen heart function.

content:

content:

title: New spectroscopy method enables direct comparisons of nuclear sizes across heavy elements
content: The size of a nucleus, defined as the nuclear charge radius, is a critical physical quantity that reflects the internal arrangement of protons and neutrons. This metric is particularly significant for deformed nuclei, such as those found in rare-earth elements, where analyzing changes in the charge radius can enhance the scientific understanding of nuclear structure and deformation.
summary: The size of a nucleus (nuclear charge radius) is an important physical quantity that reflects the arrangement of protons and neutrons within the nucleus. title: Food, fear and physics help explain group behavior from plankton to whales
content:
The open ocean presents a challenging environment characterized by patchy food distribution, abundant predators, and constantly shifting oceanographic conditions. Survival in this dynamic setting demands specific adaptations for organisms living within the pelagic environment.

This pelagic zone encompasses the offshore waters extending from the sunlit surface down through the twilight zone. The physical and biological constraints of these waters shape the behavior of marine life, ranging from microscopic plankton to large whales.
summary: The open ocean is a dynamic environment, where food is patchy, predators are plentiful, and oceanographic conditions change constantly. Life in the pelagic environment—the offshore waters that extend from the sunlit surface through the twilight zone—requires unique adaptations for survival.

However, the new system reorganizes the display of these accomplishments to improve navigation.

When browsing unlocked achievements, Steam will now separate the long list into the developer-created sets. This structure is designed to make it easier for players to see what they have completed and to find other related achievements to unlock next. Each achievement set includes its own progress bar, and completing a set awards players a "set complete" trophy that is visible on their profile.

content:

title: Scientists Discover Sun May Turn Green as Cosmic Zombie After Death
content:
Scientists have discovered the first green star, a phenomenon described as a "cosmic zombie" that aligns with the Halloween season. The discovery suggests that our Sun could potentially exhibit a similar spooky green glow in the distant future.

This hypothetical transformation would occur after the Sun's death in billions of years, at which point it may undergo a change that results in the distinctive green coloration.
summary: Scientists discovered that the Sun may go green after its death. The green glow would occur when the Sun becomes a cosmic zombie billions of years from now.

title: Klara and the Sun review – Taika Waititi’s manic pixie dream robot sci-fi is a sentimental mess
content:
Taika Waititi’s adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s novel, Klara and the Sun, has been criticized for being a "sentimental mess" that fails to offer substantial commentary on artificial intelligence, love, or grief. The director of Hunt for the Wilderpeople and Jojo Rabbit is described as creating a "twee, tiresome tale" filled with "postmodern quirkiness" and "ironic dorkiness," which the review characterizes as unbearably mannered and poorly acted.

Set in a post-World War III future where the internet has been wiped out, the film features families purchasing "artificial friend" (AF) robots for their children. The review notes technical inconsistencies in this world, such as the unclear status of AFs and the inclusion of a purple, highly flammable substance called PEC-9 in the robots' bodies. Despite Waititi’s previous success with comedy in films like Thor: Ragnarok, this project is compared unfavorably to his "fey-Hitler fantasy," Jojo Rabbit, being labeled as misjudged and self-admiring.
summary: The director of Hunt for the Wilderpeople and Jojo Rabbit turns Kazuo Ishiguro’s AI fable into a twee, tiresome tale of love and griefTaika Waititi detonates an explosion of postmodern quirkiness and ironic dorkiness in this unbearably mannered, unspeakably acted film. It’s a slice of sentimental whimsy-futurism and non-satire, adapted by Waititi from the Kazuo Ishiguro novel, which winds up saying nothing substantial or meaningful (or funny) about artificial intelligence, love or grief.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Chris Woakes criticizes England players' conduct and Rob Key's treatment
content:
Chris Woakes, a Test stalwart who has just concluded his 20th professional season, has criticized the behavior of some England players, describing their actions as “unacceptable.” The Warwickshire bowler, who recently secured his third County Championship title, addressed these issues during an interview at Edgbaston’s indoor nets on a rainy October afternoon.

Woakes’ international career included 62 Tests for England, in which he took 192 wickets and scored 2,034 runs, along with two World Cup victories. Throughout his tenure, he worked under various coaches, including Andy Flower and Brendon McCullum, and played for captains such as Sir Alastair Cook, Eoin Morgan, Joe Root, and Ben Stokes.

Reflecting on his long career, Woakes recalled advice from his parents, particularly his father, to “always be myself” when he was 17 and beginning his professional journey. The article also notes his discussions regarding his final appearance at the Oval and what he described as “shabby” treatment from Rob Key, alongside the ongoing issue of cricket’s drinking culture.
summary: Chris Woakes describes his final season at the Oval and criticizes the behavior of some England players as unacceptable. He also discusses his treatment by Rob Key and the issue of drinking culture in cricket.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Noah Sadiki scores dramatic late winner for Sunderland against Torreense
content:
Democratic Republic of the Congo midfielder Noah Sadiki scored a dramatic late goal to secure a win for Sunderland against Torreense in Portugal. With three minutes of stoppage time remaining, Sadiki half-volied the ball into the net following excellent work from Enzo Le Fée and Granit Xhaka.

The goal marked Sadiki’s first for Régis Le Bris’s side, sparking an ecstatic reaction from Sunderland supporters who had feared their celebration in Portugal might fall flat. After scoring, Sadiki hurdled a set of advertising hoardings and sprinted across a running track to join the fans.
summary: Noah Sadiki scored a dramatic late goal to secure a win for Sunderland against Torreense. The Democratic Republic of the Congo midfielder half-volleyed the ball after excellent work from Enzo Le Fée and Granit Xhaka.

content:

content: A major United Nations report intended to guide biodiversity negotiations in Armenia indicates that while nations have achieved some progress, they remain off track to meet the goal of protecting 30% of land and oceans by 2030. summary: A major UN report indicates that countries have made some progress but remain off track for the goal to protect 30% of land and oceans by 2030. This report will inform biodiversity negotiations taking place in Armenia.

title: Sports supplement may shield brain from gut inflammation damage
content:
Research suggests that a popular sports supplement may help protect the brain from damage associated with gut inflammation. The gut-brain axis functions as a two-way biochemical connection, where chronic inflammation in the gut sends inflammatory signals throughout the body that trigger neuroinflammation in the brain.

The hippocampus, the brain region responsible for memory, learning, and mood, is particularly vulnerable to this process. Disruption of the hippocampus can impact cognitive functions such as thinking and remembering, as well as emotional well-being.
summary: The gut-brain axis transmits inflammatory signals from the gut to the brain, triggering neuroinflammation. This process particularly endangers the hippocampus, which governs memory, learning, and mood.

title: Genetic testing for antidepressants does not improve treatment effectiveness
content: A clinical trial conducted in Australia by an international team of researchers found that genetic testing to select antidepressants did not result in better improvements in depressive symptoms compared to standard prescriptions based on clinical guidelines. The study evaluated whether prescribing medication based on a patient's genetic makeup offered any advantage over traditional clinical methods.
summary: An Australian clinical trial found that genetic testing to select antidepressants did not improve depressive symptoms compared to standard prescriptions. The study was conducted by an international team of researchers using clinical guidelines for the control group.

title: Alzheimer's drug access varies by race, vulnerability, and health status
content: The first disease-modifying drugs for Alzheimer's disease are designed to slow cognitive decline by targeting amyloid plaques in the brain. However, a new study indicates that patients do not have equal opportunities to receive these treatments. According to the research, race, vulnerability, and health status are key factors that shape access to the medication.
summary: New Alzheimer's drugs slow cognitive decline by targeting amyloid plaques in the brain. A new study indicates that race, vulnerability, and health status shape patient access to these treatments.

title: Harvard team develops faster antibody screening for cancer treatments
content: A research team led by scientists at Harvard Medical School, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute has developed a new antibody screening method. This approach is designed to accelerate the process of identifying and engineering cancer-fighting therapies.
summary: Researchers at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute have developed a faster method to identify cancer-fighting therapies. The antibody screening approach aims to accelerate the engineering of immune-based treatments.

title: Study finds prebiotic fiber helps girls build more bone
content:
A one-year clinical trial led by Florida International University nutrition researcher Cristina Palacios found that prebiotic fiber supplements can enhance bone development in girls. The study compared participants who added the supplement to their regular diets against a control group that received a placebo.

The results indicated that girls taking the prebiotic fiber supplement built more bone over the course of the year than those who took the placebo.
summary: A clinical trial led by Cristina Palacios at Florida International University found that girls who took a prebiotic fiber supplement for a year built more bone. The results showed these girls built more bone than girls who took a placebo.

title: Protein modification reverses cancer muscle wasting in preclinical study
content:
Cachexia, a severe form of muscle wasting affecting up to 80% of cancer patients, is driven by pro-inflammatory cytokines released by tumor cells. Known as cancer-induced cachexia (CIC), this condition is responsible for 30% to 50% of all cancer-related deaths worldwide, earning it the nickname "final disease" due to the absence of curative treatments.

A preclinical study indicates that protein modification can partially reverse this cancer-related muscle wasting, offering a potential avenue for addressing a condition currently without a cure.
summary: A preclinical study found that protein modification partially reverses cancer-related muscle wasting, known as cachexia. This condition affects up to 80% of cancer patients and is caused by pro-inflammatory signaling molecules released by tumor cells.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study links nature contact to positive food relationship
content: A study led by Anglia Ruskin University (ARU) suggests that contact with natural environments may help individuals develop healthier eating habits. Published in the journal Body Image, the research provides the first evidence that exposure to nature can influence people's relationship with food.
summary: A study led by Anglia Ruskin University found that contact with natural environments may help people develop healthier eating habits. Published in the journal Body Image, this is the first research to provide evidence that exposure to nature can influence people's relationship with food.

content:

summary: A new report from People with Disability Australia states that employers must remove barriers preventing women with disability from reaching leadership roles. Researchers in the report identify six lessons to help drive change in this area.

title: North Sea Heat Wave Triggers Underwater Plankton Bloom Missed by Satellites
content:
Satellites are frequently used by scientists to monitor ocean responses to marine heat waves by detecting changes in ocean color, which indicate shifts in phytoplankton populations. These microscopic organisms are essential to marine food webs and the global carbon cycle, yet satellite observations are limited to the ocean's surface.

In the North Sea, a recent heat wave triggered an underwater plankton bloom that was largely missed by these satellite systems due to their inability to detect activity below the surface.
summary: Scientists use satellites to detect changes in ocean color during marine heat waves. Satellites can only see the ocean's surface, missing underwater plankton blooms in the North Sea.
author: Phys.org

title: Battle of Neville's Cross: 1346 Capture of King David II Outside Durham
content:
On October 17, 1346, the Battle of Neville’s Cross took place outside Durham in northeast England. This conflict served as a decisive moment in Anglo-Scottish history, resulting in the capture of King David II of Scotland.

Despite its significant impact on relations between England, Scotland, and France, the battle remains little-known to many people.
summary: The Battle of Neville's Cross was fought on Oct. 17, 1346 outside Durham in northeast England. The battle captured King David II of Scotland, marking a decisive moment in Anglo-Scottish history.

title: AI converts scrap impurities into ingredients for stronger recycled iron
content:
AI technology is being applied to transform impurities found in scrap metal into useful ingredients that can produce stronger recycled iron.  

Global metal output reaches roughly 2 billion metric tons each year, a level that underpins industry, infrastructure and the energy sector. That scale of production accounts for an estimated 40 % of industrial greenhouse‑gas emissions and about 10 % of worldwide energy consumption.  

Expanding the use of recycled metals therefore offers a pathway to lessen the environmental footprint of metal manufacturing and to reduce dependence on imports of scarce, strategically important raw materials.
summary: AI can transform impurities in scrap metal into useful components for producing stronger recycled iron. Using more recycled metals could lower the 40% of industrial greenhouse gas emissions and 10% of global energy consumption tied to primary metal production.

title: New paper traces CDK research evolution and next-gen cancer therapies
content: A new paper traces the evolution of cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) research, marking more than 30 years since the direct connection between the molecular machinery controlling cell division and cancer was established. The study outlines the next generation of CDK-targeted therapies, extending from the initial discovery of CDK9 to applications in precision medicine and beyond.
summary: A new paper outlines the next generation of CDK-targeted therapies for cancer. The publication also traces the evolution of cyclin-dependent kinase research over more than 30 years.
author: Phys.org

title: Single 2D crystal becomes transistor with built-in insulation and contacts
content:
A new development in semiconductor technology involves a single two-dimensional crystal that transforms into a transistor with built-in insulation and electrical contacts. Traditional transistors require several fundamentally different materials, including a semiconductor to carry current, an insulating dielectric to control it, and metallic contacts for current entry and exit.

Integrating these distinct components becomes increasingly difficult as semiconductor devices approach the atomic scale. The new single-crystal approach addresses this challenge by combining the necessary functional elements within one material structure.
summary: A transistor typically requires multiple different materials, including a semiconductor, insulating dielectric, and metallic contacts. Integrating these components is difficult as semiconductor devices approach the atomic scale.

title: Building trust in governments through digital platforms
content:
Global surveys indicate that a significant portion of the population reports a lack of trust in their respective governments. This decline in confidence has been particularly notable in recent decades across Latin America, North America, and Africa.

As these regions experience falling trust levels, the focus has turned to methods for restoring public confidence. Digital platforms are being examined as a potential tool for governments to rebuild this trust with their citizens.
summary: Around the world, many people report distrusting their government. In some places, such as Latin America, North America and Africa, trust in government has declined in recent decades.

title: Satellite data offers clues on how glacial ice cliffs will collapse as climate warms
content: Scientists have not yet determined with certainty how the towering ice cliffs at the leading edges of glaciers will behave as global temperatures rise. However, recent analysis of satellite data provides initial clues regarding the stability of these glacial ice cliffs.
summary: The behavior of towering ice cliffs at the leading edge of glaciers remains uncertain as the climate warms. Satellite data provides some clues regarding how these cliffs may collapse.

content:

The findings could accelerate stem cell engineering and improve the development of disease models. Additionally, the research may inform the creation of new therapies by clarifying the mechanisms of cellular communication.
summary: A new computational approach reveals how cells communicate to assemble into tissues. This discovery could accelerate stem cell engineering, improve disease models, and inform therapies.

summary: MIT's Center for Transportation and Logistics reports that corporate sustainability commitments are at a record high. However, governance gaps and external disruptions prevent the execution of these commitments.

title: Neanderthal shoulder wound in Iraqi Kurdistan may be oldest spear kill evidence
content:
Archaeologists excavating the Shanidar cave in Iraqi Kurdistan have identified a Neanderthal adult who died more than 70,000 years ago with a smooth round hole in the shoulder blade. This distinctive injury, described as a “kill shot,” may constitute the oldest evidence to date of a human ancestor being killed by a wooden spear.

The skeletal remains of the adult and other Neanderthals were recovered from beneath nearly 8 meters of rock and sediment. The discovery provides significant insight into prehistoric hunting practices and the physical capabilities of early human ancestors.
summary: An adult Neanderthal excavated from Shanidar cave in Iraqi Kurdistan died more than 70,000 years ago with a distinctive shoulder injury. This wound may be the oldest evidence so far of a human ancestor being killed by a wooden spear.

title: NASA Satellites Track Historic 2026 El Niño Development
content: NASA is closely monitoring the development of the 2026 El Niño, a natural climate pattern characterized by warmer-than-normal water temperatures in parts of the equatorial Pacific. This phenomenon, which emerges roughly every two to seven years, is described as being rarer than a solar eclipse and more powerful than any single storm system.
summary: NASA is closely monitoring a 2026 El Niño event described as rarer than a solar eclipse and more powerful than any single storm system. This natural climate pattern involves warmer-than-normal water temperatures in parts of the equatorial Pacific and typically emerges every two to seven years.

title: NASA to Support JAXA's MMX Mission to Study Mars' Moons
content:

The primary objectives of the MMX mission are to characterize the two moons and determine their origin. Additionally, the mission is designed to deliver a sample, contributing to the scientific understanding of these celestial bodies.
summary: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA's MMX mission to advance understanding of Mars' moons. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Phobos and Deimos while delivering a sample.

title: Trump posts AI-edited photo of White House restoration work
content:
President Donald Trump shared a series of images on Truth Social highlighting renovations to the White House, including a comparison of an old column and a "restored" version. However, the restored image appears to be modified with artificial intelligence, as it was flagged by Google’s AI detector as "made or edited with OpenAI."

The step count in the after image also does not match the one in the "before" photo, and the two images appear nearly identical in angle and detail.
summary: President Donald Trump posted a series of photos on Truth Social showing White House renovations, but one image appears to be modified with AI. The photo was flagged by Google's AI detector as made or edited with OpenAI, and users noted discrepancies in the number of steps shown.

title: What did the Liberty Bell sound like? Science is on the case.
content: Researchers at Penn State Behrend investigated the acoustic properties of the Liberty Bell by conducting a modal analysis of a 20th-century replica. The study aimed to determine what the historic bell sounded like by examining the physical characteristics of the modern copy.
summary: Researchers hunted for clues in modal analysis of 20th-century replica bell at Penn State Behrend.

title: Last chance to save up to $200 on TechCrunch Founder Summit pass: Early booking ends October 16
content:
TechCrunch is ending early‑booking discounts for its Founder Summit on Friday, October 16.  Attendees can save up to $200 on Founder and Investor Passes, but the savings will vanish after the deadline.

The summit will bring together about 1,000 founders and investors on November 4 at Boston’s SoWa Power Station.  Participants are encouraged to bring their toughest questions and make the day count for their businesses.

title: Bluesky expands Attie platform to let users build interactive games, quizzes, and websites
content:
Bluesky has expanded its AI‑powered Attie app, enabling users to build a range of interactive experiences such as websites, games, and quizzes. The update is part of the platform’s broader push to make “social vibe coding” accessible to a wider audience.

According to the company, the experimental Attie platform now lets users create interactive experiences that can tap into the social network’s audience. This includes games, quizzes, and websites that can be shared and interacted with directly within Bluesky’s ecosystem.
summary: Bluesky is adding social vibe coding to its experimental Attie platform. The update lets users create interactive experiences such as games, quizzes, and websites that can tap into the social network's audience.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic Grants METR Employee-Level Access to Examine Its Operations
content:
Anthropic has granted METR researchers employee‑level access to its internal operations. The move allows the research group to examine the company’s processes in detail.

METR will publish its own assessments of Anthropic’s risks, incidents, and practices. In doing so, Anthropic has relinquished the right to block those assessments from being released.

The arrangement marks a shift in transparency for the frontier AI model maker.

title: Bluesky seeks to simplify buying, selling, and fundraising on its platform
content:
Bluesky announced plans to simplify buying, selling, and fundraising on its platform.  

During a recent executive discussion, the company emphasized that advertising is not the sole route to monetization. Executives noted that alternative models are feasible and could provide additional revenue opportunities for users and the network.
summary: Bluesky executives argue advertising is not the sole monetization path. They say alternative models are feasible for monetizing the network.
author: TechCrunch

title: Amazon Devices Chief Panos Panay Envisions AI Devices Replacing Apps
content:
Amazon devices chief Panos Panay spoke at TechCrunch Disrupt about a future in which ambient AI devices operate in the background, anticipating users’ needs without requiring explicit commands.  

Panay said that these AI devices would replace the need to use apps by continuously monitoring context and responding proactively.
summary: At TechCrunch Disrupt, Amazon devices chief Panos Panay spoke about a future where ambient AI devices operate in the background. He said these devices would anticipate users' needs instead of waiting for commands.
author: TechCrunch

title: Meta launches Muse Spark Open, an open-weight AI model for Macs
content:
Meta has announced the release of an open‑weight AI model designed to run on Mac computers. The new model, called Muse Spark Open, is set to operate locally on Apple silicon.

The launch is a joint effort between Meta and Apple. Meta’s social media platform is providing the model, while Apple will enable it to run natively on its silicon chips.

The announcement marks the first time Meta has offered an AI model that can be executed directly on Mac hardware.
summary: Meta and Apple have teamed up to launch Muse Spark Open, an open-weight AI model. The model runs locally on Apple silicon.
